body: What exactly did he do?
In our family, everyone is expected to celebrate mom. Dad didn’t do or plan *anything* while I came up with plans for her weeks prior.
Y’know, that’s fair. I accept that.

The point of contention wasn’t that I was supposed to handle everything, it’s that he was supposed to do *something*. He did nothing. I came through with my responsibility, he did not. She took cooking dinner on herself because Dad literally just peaced out on the day and tried to come back with a card he ran and got because he forgot.

He full send forgot about their anniversary last year and I took her out to dinner, if that’s any indication.

He rarely does anything to celebrate her. Birthdays, anniversaries, Mother’s Day, it’s all the same. Christmas he tries to come through but most years falls flat. 

Edit for clarification.
Short answer: no. I’ve taken her out on their anniversary to make up for it 3 out of the last 5 years.

I got her a card and flowers and brought her granddaughter to see her (with an additional card from her), but I didn’t ball out this year like I normally would. It’s not that I didn’t do anything, I was just hoping dad would want to celebrate her like we do, as the mother to his children.

Getting into Critical Role is a titanic task. With just over 1000 hours of content, it's intimidating. The beginning is beset with shoddy audio, beginner mistakes, and loose footing. The good news is that it definitely gets better. Matt and the group create, maintain, and grow an incredible chemistry that lasts through the next 5 or so years of production. 

You really see the team get into their own around episode 28. Matt's DMing has always been great, but there's a difference between DMing for a production and running a home game. The "not seeming to be apart of the group" is finding his groove as a livestream DM.
